steps.label: Shell input
steps.body: The shell reads the command and separates words according to quoting rules.

steps.label: Program + arguments
steps.body: The selected executable receives its arguments; shell syntax is not passed unchanged.

steps.label: Exit status
steps.body: The program returns an exit status and may write stdout and stderr. Check both output and status.

steps.label: Working directory
steps.body: A relative path starts at the current directory; an absolute path starts at /.

steps.label: Directory entries
steps.body: Each component selects an entry. Traversal permissions apply along the path.

steps.label: Selected file
steps.body: Read or change only the intended entry; confirm the path before a modification.

steps.label: Producer
steps.body: The first command writes bytes to standard output.

steps.label: Filter
steps.body: The pipe connects those bytes to the next command standard input; stderr remains separate unless redirected.

steps.label: Consumer
steps.body: The final stage displays or saves the transformed stream. Inspect pipeline failures as well as output.

steps.label: Identity
steps.body: The process has a user identity and group memberships.

steps.label: Permission policy
steps.body: Ownership, mode bits and additional controls determine the requested access.

steps.label: Allow or deny
steps.body: Reading a file and traversing its containing directories require different permissions.

steps.label: Measure workload
steps.body: Observe the slow task while it runs; idle measurements may miss the problem.

steps.label: Compare resources
steps.body: Compare CPU activity, available memory, disk capacity and I/O symptoms.

steps.label: Test a hypothesis
steps.body: Change one relevant condition and compare results; high utilization alone does not prove the cause.

steps.label: Package metadata
steps.body: Repository metadata describes available packages and dependencies.

steps.label: Installed files
steps.body: Installing a package places files on disk; this does not prove its service is healthy.

steps.label: Running service
steps.body: Check service state and logs independently of installation status.

steps.label: Source data
steps.body: Identify the files and the recovery point you need.

steps.label: Transfer or archive
steps.body: An archive groups files; an authenticated transfer protects the connection to the intended peer.

steps.label: Restore check
steps.body: Open or restore a sample and verify integrity. A successful copy alone is not a recovery test.

steps.label: Original bytes
steps.body: Record source and acquisition context before modifying evidence.

steps.label: Working copy
steps.body: Inspect a copy and record the tools and methods used.

steps.label: Integrity comparison
steps.body: A matching cryptographic hash supports byte equality, not the truth or origin of the contents.

steps.label: Validate inputs
steps.body: Check required arguments, paths and allowed values before doing work.

steps.label: Run one step
steps.body: Quote variables and inspect the exit status of operations that can fail.

steps.label: Stop or continue
steps.body: Handle failures explicitly and bound loops. Do not silently treat missing results as success.

steps.label: Destination address
steps.body: The application needs a route to the destination IP address.

steps.label: Route selection
steps.body: Select the most specific applicable route, subject to routing policy.

steps.label: Local delivery
steps.body: Resolve the on-link next hop when needed. An off-subnet destination normally uses a gateway link address.

steps.label: Name resolution
steps.body: If needed, obtain an address using DNS or local configuration.

steps.label: Secure connection
steps.body: Establish transport and validate the TLS peer for HTTPS. Cached connections can skip a new handshake.

steps.label: HTTP exchange
steps.body: Send a request and interpret status, headers and body. TLS success does not guarantee application correctness.

steps.label: Known scope
steps.body: Start with approved ranges and local interface and route information.

steps.label: Observed links
steps.body: Collect bounded observations and associate them with their time and measurement point.

steps.label: Annotated map
steps.body: Mark unknown devices and uncertain relationships. A missing response is not proof of absence.

steps.label: Selected probe
steps.body: Choose the target, protocol, port and scan method for the question.

steps.label: Response or timeout
steps.body: The scanner may receive a reply, rejection or no usable response.

steps.label: Inferred state
steps.body: Infer open, closed or an uncertain state for that method. An open port is not a confirmed vulnerability.

steps.label: Capture point
steps.body: Traffic visibility depends on interface, placement and capture filters.

steps.label: Saved packets
steps.body: A trace preserves observed packet bytes and timestamps; offload and loss can affect interpretation.

steps.label: Protocol analysis
steps.body: Apply display filters and follow an exchange. Absence from the capture does not prove it never occurred.

steps.label: Define endpoints
steps.body: Choose known local lab endpoints and a small measurement budget.

steps.label: Send and observe
steps.body: Record traffic and timings from the relevant observation points.

steps.label: Compare evidence
steps.body: Distinguish throughput, latency, loss and application behavior; they measure different properties.

steps.label: Input bytes
steps.body: Read a bounded file or response and handle decoding and input errors.

steps.label: Parsed values
steps.body: Convert to structured values and validate required fields before using them.

steps.label: Tested result
steps.body: Produce a reproducible summary and test malformed as well as valid input.

steps.label: Start operation
steps.body: Calling an async function returns a promise representing eventual completion.

steps.label: Await outcome
steps.body: await suspends that async function, allowing other event-loop work to proceed.

steps.label: Handle result
steps.body: Check HTTP status and parsing separately; a fulfilled fetch promise can contain an HTTP error response.

steps.label: Expected rule
steps.body: Write what each identity should be allowed to do.

steps.label: Controlled request
steps.body: Change one relevant variable and preserve the rest of the request context.

steps.label: Observed effect
steps.body: Check returned data and state changes. A status code by itself may not establish the result.

steps.label: Synthetic fixture
steps.body: Prepare known inputs with expected outcomes and no real credentials.

steps.label: Bounded program
steps.body: Set timeouts and size limits and handle errors explicitly.

steps.label: Positive + negative tests
steps.body: Confirm the intended match and a nearby non-match; explain what remains untested.

steps.label: Authentication
steps.body: Establish who is making the request.

steps.label: Object policy
steps.body: Check whether that identity may act on this object in this tenant.

steps.label: Authorized result
steps.body: Return only permitted data. A successful login does not grant access to every object.

steps.label: Untrusted data
steps.body: Treat request fields and stored user content as untrusted at the relevant boundary.

steps.label: Safe API boundary
steps.body: Use parameterized database operations or context-appropriate output handling.

steps.label: Destination context
steps.body: HTML, JavaScript, SQL and filesystem paths require different protections; one generic escape is insufficient.

steps.label: Lab browser
steps.body: Configure the intended browser to use the proxy; HTTPS inspection also needs the configured trust setup.

steps.label: Proxy inspection
steps.body: Inspect the selected request and preserve session context while changing one variable.

steps.label: Lab application
steps.body: Compare responses and server-side effects. A proxy observation alone does not confirm impact.

steps.label: Candidate input
steps.body: Start with scoped names, paths or technology hints.

steps.label: Tool observation
steps.body: A tool reports behavior under its filters, access and timing conditions.

steps.label: Manual validation
steps.body: Check ownership, false positives and application context before treating a candidate as a finding.

steps.label: Local request
steps.body: Use the synthetic server and explicit timeout and response-size limits.

steps.label: Response checks
steps.body: Inspect the exact headers or fields that the utility is designed to assess.

steps.label: Limited conclusion
steps.body: A missing header is an observation. It does not prove an exploitable vulnerability or complete security.

steps.label: Business invariant
steps.body: State the property that must remain true across requests, caches or services.

steps.label: Boundary interaction
steps.body: Consider concurrency, parser differences or cached state where assumptions can diverge.

steps.label: Invariant retest
steps.body: Check the resulting state and legitimate behavior after the repair, not only one response.

steps.label: Question and scope
steps.body: Specify the asset and the uncertainty you want to resolve.

steps.label: Focused observation
steps.body: Select one suitable tool or extension and bound generated traffic.

steps.label: Correlated evidence
steps.body: Compare observations with application behavior and known configuration before drawing a conclusion.

steps.label: Pattern or contract
steps.body: A template, source rule or API contract defines a limited check.

steps.label: Candidate result
steps.body: A match may lack reachability, runtime context or business impact.

steps.label: Validation + retest
steps.body: Trace the data flow, establish the relevant effect and verify the fix with negative controls.

steps.label: Baseline
steps.body: Record scope, versions, configuration and expected behavior.

steps.label: Assessment
steps.body: Collect evidence using checks relevant to that baseline.

steps.label: Remediation verification
steps.body: Prioritize supported findings and repeat the relevant checks after repair.

steps.label: Service identity
steps.body: Confirm the endpoint, protocol and intended role.

steps.label: Configuration evidence
steps.body: Inspect allowed authentication, protocol and cryptographic settings in context.

steps.label: Retest result
steps.body: Verify corrected behavior while ensuring legitimate clients still work.

steps.label: Scoped search
steps.body: Query the existing index for assets within your approved scope.

steps.label: Recorded banner
steps.body: Read observation time, address and service details; data may be stale or inferred.

steps.label: Asset verification
steps.body: Verify current ownership and configuration before reporting an exposure. Search is not a live login or scan.

steps.label: Select module
steps.body: Read its description and understand whether it scans, checks or performs another operation.

steps.label: Configure context
steps.body: Review target, required options and inherited global settings in the correct console.

steps.label: Interpret result
steps.body: A completed job is not necessarily a session or confirmed weakness. Module capabilities differ.

steps.label: Alice requests Bob data
steps.body: The synthetic request targets an invoice owned by another user and tenant.

steps.label: Policy decision
steps.body: Vulnerable mode omits the required object restriction; fixed mode checks identity and tenant.

steps.label: Compare modes
steps.body: The fixture changes the unauthorized read to 403 while legitimate owner access stays available.

steps.label: Pending session
steps.body: Login creates an incomplete session; protected routes must reject it.

steps.label: MFA transition
steps.body: Fixed mode accepts the training second factor and rotates the token.

steps.label: Completed session
steps.body: The new token works; the old token, logged-out token and expired token must fail.

steps.label: Shared unused state
steps.body: Two requests both want to redeem one coupon.

steps.label: Critical decision
steps.body: An unprotected check then update can admit both; the fixed local fixture uses one locked decision.

steps.label: One success
steps.body: Verify exactly one successful redemption and one rejection. A process lock does not coordinate multiple servers.

steps.label: Entry point
steps.body: Find where external input and the authenticated identity enter the route.

steps.label: Data access
steps.body: Follow how the object is selected and which permission check protects it.

steps.label: Regression assertion
steps.body: Write one allowed case and one forbidden case that expose the root cause.

steps.label: Message event
steps.body: The browser supplies origin, source and message data.

steps.label: Boundary checks
steps.body: Compare expected origin and source, then validate message shape and allowed type.

steps.label: Safe display
steps.body: Use textContent for the accepted text. Passing unit tests does not prove browser CSP enforcement.

steps.label: Asset and actor
steps.body: Name the protected data and the identities that can approach it.

steps.label: Trust boundary
steps.body: Mark where identity, input or data crosses a change in trust.

steps.label: Control and evidence
steps.body: State the abuse case, repair and test that would demonstrate the intended rule.

steps.label: Positive control
steps.body: Run assertions against the fixed fixture and preserve legitimate behavior.

steps.label: Negative control
steps.body: Apply fixed expectations to the vulnerable fixture and confirm that they detect its weakness.

steps.label: Coverage statement
steps.body: Document what the assertions cover and the browser or integration checks that remain manual.

steps.label: Reproduction
steps.body: Record synthetic scope, prerequisites and a minimal repeatable observation.

steps.label: Root cause and repair
steps.body: Explain the missing rule and the change that restores it.

steps.label: Retest evidence
steps.body: Compare repaired and legitimate cases and record limits in the report.

steps.label: Persistent storage
steps.body: Programs and files remain on SSD or HDD after normal shutdown.

steps.label: Working memory
steps.body: The OS loads active data into RAM; cache holds smaller frequently used portions near execution.

steps.label: CPU execution
steps.body: The CPU executes instructions using the memory hierarchy. This is a simplified data path, not a timing model.

steps.label: Application request
steps.body: A user program requests a protected operation through an OS interface.

steps.label: Kernel mediation
steps.body: The kernel checks access and manages resources and device drivers.

steps.label: Operation result
steps.body: The program receives data or an error. The shell is a user program, not the kernel.

steps.label: Host filesystem
steps.body: Physical host storage contains the virtual disk file and other host files.

steps.label: Virtual block device
steps.body: The hypervisor presents virtual capacity to the guest; file allocation may grow over time.

steps.label: Guest filesystem
steps.body: Guest partitions and filesystems have their own sizes and free space; enlarging one layer does not resize every layer.

steps.label: Application + transport
steps.body: Application bytes are carried by a transport protocol such as TCP or UDP.

steps.label: IP packet
steps.body: An IP envelope supports delivery across networks.

steps.label: Link frame
steps.body: The link layer carries the packet to the next hop. Routers replace the link envelope for subsequent links.

steps.label: Prefix length
steps.body: A /26 leaves six host bits, giving blocks of 64 IPv4 addresses.

steps.label: Containing block
steps.body: 70 lies in the .64 through .127 block; the mask is 255.255.255.192.

steps.label: Host range
steps.body: For this conventional subnet, .65 through .126 are 62 host addresses. /31 and /32 differ.

steps.label: Interface + route
steps.body: Check link state, addresses and the selected path before blaming an application.

steps.label: Name + transport
steps.body: Separate name resolution from reaching the intended listener and port.

steps.label: TLS + application
steps.body: Distinguish certificate validation, HTTP error status and incorrect application data.
